This Misc. Appeal has been filed by the appellant/Insurance Company assailing the impugned award dated 18.11.2019 passed by the learned Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal at Bijawar, District Chhatarpur in Claim Case No. 48/2016 Smt. Kaushalya and ors. v. R. Sarvanan Godar and another filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.

sentences.text:
2. In short, the facts of case are that on 06.05.2016, Truck No. TN- 24/H/9172, allegedly being driven at high speed and negligently by respondent No. 9 dashed against Bhupendra Singh,
therefore, he received fatal injuries and died.
Accordingly, claim was filed by the respondents No. 1 to 8.

After recording of the evidence, issues were framed and after appreciating the material on record, the learned tribunal awarded compensation of Rs. 22,82,680/-.
3.

Against the award, the appellant/insurance company has argued that regarding income,
employment and age of the deceased evidence was tendered by Chattar Singh, who claimed to be an Account Manager in Bansal Construction Company.

He admitted that he had not issued any Branch Manager vs Smt. Kaushalay on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70356440/
2 appointment letter.
Therefore, status of Chattar Singh is not clear.
He further admitted that he did not have any authorization letter to issue certificate (Ex. P-13), therefore, income of the deceased could not have been taken as Rs. 11,700/-.
The learned tribunal has erred in calculating the monthly income of the deceased on the premises that deceased was getting Rs. 2,200/- per month in 22 days for daily expenses.
Therefore, the amount is exhorbitant and the same should be suitably reduced.
4. At the time of final hearing, respondent Nos. 1 to 8, supported the award of the learned Tribunal.

5. Heard the learned counsel of rival parties and perused the record of the Tribunal.
6.
The question before this Court is whether any interference can be made in the award dated 18.11.2019 passed in Claim Case No. 48/2016.
7. This appeal has been filed by the appellant/insurance company only on the ground of quantum.

P.W.-3 (Chattar Singh), Account Manager, Bansal Construction Company has deposed that the deceased was working as a skilled worker in Bansal Construction Company on the date of accident i.e. is 06.05.2016 and was being paid Rs. 11,700/- per month.
But, assuming it to be Rs. 8,435/- for a skilled compressor man that was deceased on 06.05.2016 i.e. date of death, under the provisions of minimum wages in M.P., calculation can be made.

In the case of Reshma Kumari v. Madan Mohan and anr. 2013 ACJ 1253, Volume 9, it has been held that where the dependents of married deceased person are more than six, then only 1/5th deduction should be made but the learned trial Court has although found the dependents to be more than 6 persons, however, has deducted 1/3rd of income for the expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: Reshma Kumari v. Madan Mohan and anr. 2013 ACJ 1253, Volume 9
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, deducting income by 1/5th from the assumed income of Rs. 8,435 p.m. x 12 = 1,01,220/- (annual income), the dependency of 8 dependents comes to Rs. 80,976/- after deducting 1/5 th income as expense of deceased.
As the deceased was aged between 26 to 30 years as held correctly by learned Tribunal in Para-23 of judgment by applying multiplier of 17, this dependency comes to Rs.13,76,592/-.

In this amount, if we add 40 % for future growth, this amount would come to Rs. 19,27,228.80/-.
8.

In the above calculated compensation amount of Rs. 19,27,228.80/-, if in the light of judgments of Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others (2018) 18 SCC 130, United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Satinder Kaur 2020 ACJ 2131 (S.C.)
and New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs. Somwati and others 2020 ACJ 2321 (paras 38, 39, 40, 42 and 43).

sentences.text:
On adding Rs. 15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs. 15,000/- for loss of estate, plus Rs.44,000 x 8 for loss of consortium- loss of spousal consortium, parental consortium and loss of love and affection of child to parents as filial consortium which the Claims Tribunal has not awarded, the total amount becomes 23,09,228.80/-.
9.

Therefore, the quantum of amount of compensation of Rs. 22,82,680/- as determined by the learned trial Court, is in fact less than the calculated amount of Rs. 23,09,228.80/-, therefore, no interference can be made in the quantum of the compensation for reducing it further in an appeal of insurance company.
10. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
